findings.evidence: Lines 63–77 define the equivalence and then define the map as exactly that equivalence; lines 87–105 expose `one` and `mul` only for the duplicate map, while the only inverse-facing packaged law is `tangentAd_inv` at lines 309–310 under stronger C³ and completeness assumptions.
findings.fix: Remove the separate map definition, state `one`, `mul`, and `inv` directly for `adjointContinuousLinearEquiv`, and use its coercion in application and bracket lemmas.
findings.issue: `adjointContinuousLinearMap` duplicates the coercion of `adjointContinuousLinearEquiv`, splitting the public API; moreover `one`/`mul` are supplied only for this weaker wrapper and no inverse law characterizes the equivalence at C¹ regularity.

summary: The differential is exposed through a redundant weaker wrapper, while its canonical continuous equivalence lacks the group-action API available under the same C¹ assumptions.
